title: (Senior) Flight Safety Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Mission Brief 

At Isar Aerospace, we are enabling affordable and flexible access to space. As Europe’s leading privately funded launch company, we are developing and operating launch vehicles that provide reliable access to orbit for commercial and institutional customers worldwide. 

To support the continued development and operation of our launch systems, we are looking for a (Senior) Flight Safety Engineer to take ownership of flight safety engineering activities across vehicle development, licensing, and launch operations. In this role, you will drive the flight safety framework for our launch vehicles and act as a key interface between engineering, regulatory authorities, and launch range partners. 

As a (Senior) Flight Safety Engineer in the Mission and Launch operations team, you will work at the intersection of engineering, risk analysis and mission operations. In that frame, you will ensure that our launch systems meet the highest standards of safety, reliability, and regulatory compliance throughout the vehicle lifecycle. 

Your Role in Our Space Mission 

  • Own system-level flight safety engineering activities for launch vehicle development and operations.  
  • Define, manage, and verify system requirements related to Range Safety Systems (RTS) and Flight Termination Systems (FTS), ensuring compliance with range and regulatory requirements.  
  • Support mission licensing activities and regulatory approvals, including preparation of safety analyses and compliance documentation.  
  • Coordinate with RAMS department to perform Functional Hazard Assessments (FHA), Failure Modes and Effects Analyses (FMEA), Failure Modes, Effects and Criticality Analyses (FMECA) to support the safety case.  
  • Coordinate closely with Avionics, GNC, Flight Software, Propulsion, Structures, and Operations teams to ensure safety requirements are properly integrated into system design.  
  • Support the development, maintenance, and validation of debris and fragmentation models to assess flight safety risks and support mission approvals.  
  • Support flight safety analyses including trajectory risk assessments, casualty expectation calculations, and launch commit criteria development.  
  • Contribute to anomaly investigations, root cause analyses, and continuous improvement of flight safety methodologies and processes.  
  • Support the evolution of Isar Aerospace's flight safety standards, tools, and engineering practices. 

Qualification Checklist 

  • Master's degree or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline.  
  • Minimum 5 years of professional experience in launch vehicle flight safety, system safety, reliability engineering, launch vehicle development, missile systems, or a comparable aerospace environment.  
  • Strong experience with 14 CFR Part 450 and its application to launch licensing, hazard analysis, and public safety requirements.  
  • Demonstrated experience with FHA, FMEA, FMECA, fault tree analysis (FTA), reliability assessments, and safety case development.  
  • Experience working with RTS/FTS architectures, range safety requirements, and launch operations.  
  • Ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary engineering organizations and influence technical decisions.  
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a pragmatic engineering mindset.  
  • Excellent communication skills in English. 

Bonus Skills

  • Experience working with commercial launch providers, defence programs, or space agencies.  
  • Familiarity with 14 CFR part 450 (RCC319, 321 and 324) or equivalent licensing processes.  
  • Knowledge of Monte Carlo-based risk assessments, quantitative risk analysis and casualty expectation analyses.  
  • Basics of RF engineering and antenna systems 
  • Experience developing or reviewing fragmentation, debris, and risk assessment models for aerospace applications. 
  • Experience supporting launch campaigns and mission readiness reviews.  
  • Familiarity with ECSS, NASA, FAA, or range safety standards and practices.  
  • Programming skills in Python, MATLAB, or similar analytical environments.

  • 30 days of vacation: Enjoy the days off to relax and recharge
  • Company pension plan: Secure your future with our company pension plan, featuring a 20% employer contribution after the probation period

  • And Much More! Discover additional perks and benefits when you join our team

We are Isar Aerospace and we are at the forefront of New Space building a modern space business to enable faster, better and cheaper access to space.

Our mission is to help democratise space and use it for good in order to improve life on Earth now and for the future generations.

We are a fast-growing company aiming to provide sustainable and environmentally friendly launch solutions for small and medium-sized satellites and constellations into Low Earth Orbit.
